title: Differentiate between $_GET and $_POST Methods in PHP
summaryPoint: Two primary PHP superglobal request arrays used for collecting submitted form data.
keyPoints: $_GET passes form field values visible as query parameters in the browser address bar, has a character limit, and should not be used for sensitive credentials.
$_POST bundles form data securely inside the HTTP request payload body without exposing values in the URL.
$_GET allows search URLs to be bookmarked, while $_POST is used for sensitive submissions such as passwords and monetary transactions.

title: Differentiate between Indexed Arrays and Associative Arrays in PHP
summaryPoint: Indexed arrays use numeric indices starting from 0, whereas associative arrays use named string keys.
keyPoints: Indexed Arrays assign sequential numeric indexes automatically or manually starting at index 0 (e.g. $fruits = array('Apple', 'Banana')).
Associative Arrays utilize named string identifiers as indices associated with specific values (e.g. $age = array('Peter' => 35)).
Indexed array items are accessed via numerical indexes ($arr[0]), while associative arrays are accessed via string keys ($arr['key']).

title: Explain Rules for Variable Declaration and Data Types in PHP
summaryPoint: Variables in PHP are loosely typed identifiers prefixed with the dollar ($) sign.
keyPoints: A variable name must begin with the $ sign, followed immediately by a letter or an underscore, and cannot start with a number.
Variable names are case-sensitive ($var and $VAR are treated as distinct storage containers).
PHP automatically associates a data type based on the assigned value (Integer, Float, String, Boolean, Array, Object, NULL).

title: Explain User-Defined Functions in PHP with Syntax
summaryPoint: Reusable subroutines defined using the function keyword that execute upon invocation.
keyPoints: A function is defined using the keyword function followed by the function name, parentheses, and a code block: function functionName($param) { ... }.
Functions can receive input arguments by value or reference and return values to the caller using the return statement.
Functions promote modularity, eliminate redundant code, and run only when explicitly called.
